tweets.text:
I find the social trading dilemma quite interesting. 

If you have a large following whether you like it or not people will track your wallet, fomo/pump accounts, and every move you make will get scrutinized. 

But the treatment of these people is split online. 

Some people are revered as god tier onchain traders. 

Others are shit on for “farming”. 

The interesting part is some of the people viewed as the best are the actual ones farming. 

While there are others just trading a single public account get shit on because people simply don’t like them. 

It seems like a no win scenario.

You either accept that Twitter is going to watch your every move or don’t tie your public persona to these apps which eliminates a lot of their upside.

tweets.text:
Bitcoin pumpers are trying to hitch Bitcoin to the AI wagon, hoping investors will see it as part of the AI trade. They have it backwards. AI isn’t bullish for Bitcoin; it’s a threat to it.

AI competes with Bitcoin for speculative capital, electricity, and data-center infrastructure. Plus, as AI becomes more powerful, it could discover vulnerabilities in Bitcoin’s code, cryptography, wallets, or network that humans have missed. Bitcoin’s security and protocol-enforced scarcity ultimately depend on software remaining secure.
